0 Lata Lata is a strategic board game for 1–4 players set in Portugal's thriving canning industry of the 1950s. As the owner of a local cannery, you'll compete to produce and sell premium sardine and mackerel preserves, carefully managing fish, olive oil, and tomato supplies while expanding your factory. Each round features a clever action-point auction: sacrifice actions to secure the best resources, or keep more actions to maximize production. Balancing these decisions is the key to reaching lucrative markets, earning money, and collecting valuable scorecards that determine your final victory points. Combining resource management, bidding, and engine building, Lata offers meaningful strategic choices inspired by an iconic chapter of Portuguese industrial history. community_text:
[Rating: 3/10] Scoring system feels very random. Don't like the action selection system, which can lead to completely action-less rounds. Felt bad / unenjoyable in the majority of my playthroughs (around 10).

[Rating: 4/10] This probably works OK with two, but with three it has the potential for a serious fallaway trailer problem. Once behind you have the great choice between bidding high and not having enough actions to complete orders, or bidding low and getting stuck with bad cards you are required to place.

[Rating: 4/10] Tried at PAX Unplugged '24.  Dry eurogame in a small box, with a length ly manual.  Didn't give it enough time to learn strategy.

[Rating: 4/10] While my first play of Lata felt like I was discovering something new and exciting, I now feel like I was simply tricked by the game's phase structure and the quirky spatial wrinkle of its production engine. All the excitement happens during the bidding phase, and after that I'm just waiting (far too long) for everyone to figure out the optimal card picks on their turns.

[Rating: 4.5/10] Not a bad game, but it is just a frustrating one. You play against the players and the game, which is almost always not a great thing to deal with. Money is really important, making for a more truncated play instead of fun.

[Rating: 5/10] Me esperaba un producto similar a Café, que me encanta. Pero este juego es más enrevesado y lioso. Ninguna ventaja para mantenerlo. Vendido.

[Rating: 5/10] The theme is great and the art and components are excellent. Really love the shiny cards! I played this 5 times solo. As a solo game it is not that interesting. The choices in the game are pretty obvious and it is fairly easy to achieve a high score. For a short solo game it felt repetative and a bit dull to me. The variation in the companies is nice, but not enough to keep my interest. I really like café, not a fan of this one.
